11.text: BOATS. — The large skin boats used by the Chukchee and the Asiatic

12.text: Eskimo are very similar to those of arctic America in shape and in details

13.text: of construction. The differences are not greater than those between boats of

14.text: the western and eastern Eskimo, especially since whole frames and parts of

15.text: them have been carried from ancient times across Bering Strait as objects for

16.text: sale. The Koryak boats, with their flaring sides and semicircular stern and

17.text: bow, on the contrary, form a quite separate type; while the Kamchadal have

18.text: no skin boats, but use instead dug-outs with planks fastened to the upper edges.

19.text: The reason for this does not rest exclusively with the difference of the

20.text: natural surroundings of the tribes mentioned. It is true, that with the Chuk-

21.text: chee the scarcity of wood sufficiently explains their predilection for the skin

22.text: boat, but the Koryak shore abounds in large trunks of driftwood suitable for

23.text: building wooden boats. On the other hand, the shores of Kamchatka are

24.text: probably even richer in sea-mammals than those of the Chukchee Peninsula,

25.text: and thus afford every convenience for constructing skin boats. The Kamchadal,

26.text: nevertheless, remain a fishing tribe, with clumsy wooden canoes; and they have

27.text: never shown much skill in maritime pursuits, although they crave blubber and

28.text: hides as much as do their northern neighbors.

29.text: The Chukchee and the Asiatic Eskimo cover their boats with walrus-hide,

30.text: which is split for the purpose, one thin strip being left intact for joining the

31.text: halves. The walrus-hide is so large that a skin and a half suffice to cover

32.text: the largest boat. The specimen in the American Museum of Natural History

33.text: is thirty-five feet long and is covered with less than two skins. Ground-seal

34.text: skin, though quite suitable for boat-coverings, is never used because of its

35.text: great value for thongs and soles. The Koryak, on the contrary, cover their

36.text: boats with skins of the Okhotsk variety of ground-seal, having indeed no other

37.text: material. I have never heard of large Chukchee boats, being made of skins

38.text: of smaller seals. The Koryak, and especially the Kerek, sometimes have
